title: In a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring the number of minimal primes is bounded by the length of the quotient by an element avoiding them

standard_prerequisites.name: Support of a finite module and finite length for a module supported at the closed point
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows Q has finite length and hence is annihilated by a power of x.

standard_prerequisites.name: The snake lemma applied to a square of multiplication maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the exact sequence relating R/x^nR, M/x^nM and Q, which yields the length equality.

standard_prerequisites.name: The one-dimensional length lemma for the quotients R_i/xR_i
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the length equality into the explicit alternating count from which the bound follows.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where R is reduced: set R' = R/sqrt(0) = R/(cap_i p_i), note that R' has the same t minimal primes, and that R'/xR' is a surjective image of R/xR so its length is smaller (proof lines 38024-38030).
For reduced R with minimal primes p_1, ..., p_t, use the exact sequence 0 -> R -> prod_i R/p_i -> Q -> 0 and write M = prod_i R/p_i (proof lines 38033-38041).

Localize at p_j to see that R_{p_j} -> M_{p_j} = (R/p_j)_{p_j} is surjective, hence Q_{p_j} = 0 for all j, so that the support of Q is the single prime m and Q has finite length (proof lines 38042-38052).
Since the support of Q is m, pick n large enough that x^n acts as zero on Q (proof lines 38053-38056).

Apply the snake lemma to the displayed commutative square whose vertical maps are multiplication by x^n, noting that these are injective on R and on M because x lies in no p_i, and obtain the exact sequence 0 -> Q -> R/x^nR -> M/x^nM -> Q -> 0 (proof lines 38057-38071).
Read off length_R(R/x^nR) = length_R(M/x^nM) for large n, and decompose the latter as sum_i length_R(R_i/x^nR_i) with R_i = R/p_i (proof lines 38072-38075).

Apply the one-dimensional length lemma and use that x is a nonzerodivisor on R and on each R_i to get n length_R(R/xR) = sum_i n length_{R_i}(R_i/x R_i); conclude t <= length_R(R/xR) since each summand on the right is at least 1 (proof lines 38076-38082).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension 1, an element x in m not contained in any minimal prime of R, and the number t of minimal primes, and asserts t <= length_R(R/xR) (source lines 38015-38021). The proof first reduces to the reduced case: putting R' = R/sqrt(0), the ring R' has the same number t of minimal primes and its quotient R'/xR' is a surjective image of R/xR, hence has smaller length (proof lines 38024-38030). For reduced R the proof uses the exact sequence 0 -> R -> prod_i R/p_i -> Q -> 0, computes that Q localized at any p_j vanishes, so that the support of Q is the single prime m, which makes Q of finite length and killed by a power x^n of x (proof lines 38033-38056). The substantive computation is then the snake lemma applied to the displayed square of multiplication-by-x^n maps: because x is not in any p_i, multiplication by x^n is injective on R and on M, and the snake sequence gives 0 -> Q -> R/x^nR -> M/x^nM -> Q -> 0, whence length_R(R/x^nR) = length_R(M/x^nM) for large n (proof lines 38057-38072). Splitting M as the product of the R_i = R/p_i and applying the one-dimensional polynomial-length lemma with x a nonzerodivisor gives n length_R(R/xR) = sum_i n length_{R_i}(R_i/xR_i), and since each term on the right is at least 1 the bound t <= length_R(R/xR) follows (proof lines 38073-38082). The non-routine steps are the support computation for Q and the snake-lemma length identity.
